title: Query-Conditioned Marginals for OT-Based Context Compression: An Empirical Investigation

contributions.purpose: Make optimal-transport context compression query-aware so capacity is not wasted on task-irrelevant tokens.
contributions.mechanism: QCap-OT, an inference-only modification that reweights the OT sender marginals in Sinkhorn-based ComprExIT according to query-anchor similarity, requiring no retraining or additional parameters.
contributions.evaluation: Experiments show QCap-OT is statistically indistinguishable from vanilla ComprExIT (F1 delta approximately 0, p > 0.05) across all metrics.
contributions.source_quote: We propose QCap-OT, an inference-only method for query-conditioned OT compression that requires no retraining or additional parameters.

contributions.purpose: Rigorously test whether query-conditioned reweighting improves OT-based compression.
contributions.mechanism: Empirical comparison of QCap-OT against vanilla ComprExIT with statistical significance testing.
contributions.evaluation: QCap-OT does not improve over ComprExIT (F1 delta approximately 0, p > 0.05); a negative result.
contributions.domain: extractive question answering with compressed contexts
contributions.source_quote: We provide empirical evaluation showing QCap-OT does not improve over ComprExIT in our experiments, with rigorous statistical testing.

contributions.purpose: Alert the community to a reproducibility problem in context compression research.
contributions.mechanism: Documented re-implementation of ComprExIT with extensive debugging against published results.
contributions.evaluation: The re-implementation achieves only 2.47% F1 on SQuAD versus the published 68.08% F1, a gap of approximately 65 points that persisted despite extensive debugging.
contributions.source_quote: We document a significant reproducibility challenge in context compression research, highlighting the importance of code release for validating novel methods.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Our work builds on ComprExIT by introducing query-conditioned marginals to bias compression toward task-relevant information.
Our approach differs by modifying the optimal transport marginals rather than the token selection mechanism, enabling query conditioning without retraining the compression model.

notes: Explicit negative-result paper: proposed method statistically indistinguishable from baseline, and the finding is confounded by a failed reproduction of the ComprExIT baseline (2.47% vs published 68.08% F1). Contributions bullet list on page 2.
